notes.text: These men are — A great truth: but St. Paul did not need, nor would accept, of such testimony.
The magistrates — The supreme magistrates of the city. In the next verse they are called by a title which often signifies pretors. These officers exercised both the military and civil authority.
Being Jews — A nation peculiarly despised by the Romans.

And teach customs which it is not lawful for us to receive — The world has received all the rules and doctrines of all the philosophers that ever were. But this is a property of Gospel truth: it has something in it peculiarly intolerable to the world.

They laid many stripes upon them — Either they did not immediately say they were Romans, or in the tumult it was not regarded. Charging the jailer - Perhaps rather to quiet the people than because they thought them criminal.

Secured their feet in the stocks — These were probably those large pieces of wood, in use among the Romans, which not only loaded the legs of the prisoner, but also kept them extended in a very painful manner.
Paul and Silas sung a hymn to God — Notwithstanding weariness, hunger stripes, and blood. And the prisoners heard - A song to which they were not accustomed.

But Paul cried — As they were all then in the dark, it is not easy to say, how Paul knew of the jailer's purpose; unless it were by some immediate notice from God, which is by no means incredible. With a loud voice - Through earnestness, and because he was at some distance. Do thyself no harm - Although the Christian faith opens the prospect into another life, yet it absolutely forbids and effectually prevents a man's discharging himself from this.

Sirs — He did not style them so the day before. What must I do to be saved? - From the guilt I feel and the vengeance I fear? Undoubtedly God then set his sins in array before him, and convinced him in the clearest and strongest manner that the wrath of God abode upon him.
Thou shalt be saved and thy household — If ye believe. They did so, and were saved.

He washed their stripes — It should not be forgot, that the apostles had not the power of working miraculous cures when they pleased, either on themselves, or their dearest friends. Nor was it expedient they should, since it would have frustrated many wise designs of God, which were answered by their sufferings.
He set a table before them and rejoiced — Faith makes a man joyful, prudent, liberal.

glossa.text: *Following Paul. ((ID.))* Although she had met them, the woman cries out not to their face, but behind them, keeping modesty.

*They cast them into prison. ((ID.))* By this the power of the deliverer is the greater. To the same purpose looks also that which follows: *He put into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.*
*And at midnight,* etc. Prayer is to be made at midnight, and in dangers the diligence of prayer is to be kept.

*A great earthquake was made,* etc. The devotion of them that pray and the power of prayer is expressed, because while they sing hymns in the prison their praise moves the earth: it shakes the foundations of the prison, opens the doors, looses the chains of the bound.

*He fell down,* etc. ((RAB.)) On account of power and knowledge: power, because by the earthquake the doors were opened: knowledge, because Paul knew why he wished to kill himself: therefore before all he fell down at the feet of Paul and Silas.

*He washed their stripes. ((BED.))* A beautiful variety of things. Those whose stripes of wounding he washed, through them he lost the stripes of his crime. *Immediately. ((RAB.))* The swiftness of obedience is betokened. The grace of the Holy Spirit knows no slow endeavours.
*And when he had brought them, he set a table before them,* etc. ((ID.)) An excellent example of both: the entering of the house, and the setting of the table.

notes.text: Isles — The Gentile nations, as this word, used Isaiah xlii, 4, is expounded, Matt. xii, 21.
Darkness — A dark cloud doth encompass him.
Heavens — The angels, yea God himself from heaven.
Confounded — Let them be ashamed of their folly. Gods - All you whom the Gentiles have made the objects of their worship.
Zion — Thy people dwelling in Zion or Jerusalem, to whom Christ came. Heard - The fame of thy judgments, and the setting up the kingdom of the Messiah.
Light — Joy and happiness. Sown - Is laid up for them. This psalm sets forth the glory of the Redeemer, ver. 1-3. And the joy of the redeemed, ver. 4-9. A psalm.

glossa.text:
*The Lord hath reigned.* ((CASS.)) The prophet, seeing the superstitions of the world abound before the resurrection of Christ, sets against them: *The Lord hath reigned.* ((AUG.)) Who then is another to be worshipped? as it were, none; thereupon:

*Let the earth rejoice.* What remains to the idols? As it were, nothing.

*The islands.* The Churches of the whole world. *Many.* Not all, because of the assemblies of the heretics.

((CASS.)) Thereupon he tells what manner of Lord he is in the first coming.

*Clouds and darkness.* To the wicked, who are blind, he is cloudy and dark, to whom he shines with no brightness; but to the good, *Justice and judgment.* They who are corrected are his seat. Before his coming *fire shall go before,* because the wicked, kindled with wrath at the preaching of the prophets, took counsel of their slaying, and were inflamed unto indignation round about, because they were many, whereas the preachers were few.
*Fire shall go before him,* etc. ((AUG.)) As it were, they who are corrected are the seat of God, etc., *as far as* if they are wicked, unto consuming; if good, unto repairing.
*His lightnings have shone forth.* ((ID.)) The clouds grew cheap in their human form, but a wondrous brightness appeared in their words or deeds, and thereupon the earth was moved.
*They flowed down.* ((ID.)) Even if the pagan does not believe just now, yet he is overcome.
*Let them be confounded.* This has now been done. ((AUG.)) For idolatry now ceases. And let them blush who adore stones, because they are dead.

*Adore ye.* ((ID.)) The adoration of the angels therefore ceases, but they adore. The evil angels themselves wish to be adored, the good adore, and do not suffer themselves to be adored. Or at least by this example let idolatry cease.

 *I have heard and she was glad.* ((CASS.)) Secondly, after the restoration of the land, an exultation of every kind, etc., *as far as* as the brethren rejoiced over Cornelius, whom Peter baptized. *And they rejoiced.* ((AUG.)) The apostles heard, who were brethren in Judaea, that the Gentiles had received the word of God, and they were glad and magnified God.
*The earth . . . the gods.* ((ID.)) By *the earth* and *the gods* understand sinners and just men. Or, he signifies that he rules over things earthly and things heavenly.

*The Lord keepeth.* ((AUG.)) If, when thou hast begun to hate the malignant, persecutions follow after, fear not, because the Lord keeps the souls of his saints, for the taking away of whom is the last kind of persecution.

notes.text: I — Jesus Christ. Come quickly - To judge the world. And my reward is with me - The rewards which I assign both to the righteous and the wicked are given at my coming. To give to every man according as his work - His whole inward and outward behaviour shall be.
I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last — Who exist from everlasting to everlasting. How clear, incontestable a proof, does our Lord here give of his divine glory!

Happy are they that do his commandments — His, who saith, I come - He speaks of himself. That they may have right - Through his gracious covenant. To the tree of life - To all the blessings signified by it. When Adam broke his commandment, he was driven from the tree of life. They who keep his commandments "shall eat thereof."

I Jesus have sent my angel to testify these things — Primarily. To you - The seven angels of the churches; then to those churches - and afterwards to all other churches in succeeding ages. I - as God. Am the root - And source of David's family and kingdom; as man, an descended from his loins. "I am the star out of Jacob," Num. xxiv, 17; like the bright morning star, who put an end to the night of ignorance, sin, and sorrow, and usher in an eternal day of light, purity, and joy.

The Spirit and the bride — The Spirit of adoption in the bride, in the heart of every true believer. Say - With earnest desire and expectation. Come - And accomplish all the words of this prophecy. And let him that thirsteth, come - Here they also who are farther off are invited. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life - He may partake of my spiritual and unspeakable blessings, as freely as he makes use of the most common refreshments; as freely as he drinks of the running stream.

He that testifieth these things — Even all that is contained in this book. Saith - For the encouragement of the church in all her afflictions. Yea - Answering the call of the Spirit and the bride. I come quickly - To destroy all her enemies, and establish her in a state of perfect and everlasting happiness. The apostle expresses his earnest desire and hope of this, by answering, Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!

The grace — The free love. Of the Lord Jesus - And all its fruits. Be with all - Who thus long for his appearing! It may be proper to subjoin here a short view of the whole contents of this book. In the year of the world, 3940. Jesus Christ is born, three years before the common computation. In that which is vulgarly called, the thirtieth year of our Lord, Jesus Christ dies; rises; ascends. Year (A.D.) Event As Described In Revelation Chapter/Verse 96 The Revelation is given; the coming of our Lord is declared to the seven churches in Asia, and their angels, Rev i., ii., iii. 97, 98 The seven seals are opened, and under the fifth the chronos is declared, iv.-vi. Seven trumpets are given to the seven angels, vii. viii. Century, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th, the trumpet of the 1st, 2d, 3d, 4th angel, viii. 510-589 The first woe, \............... 589-634 The interval after the first woe} ix...... 634-840 The second woe, /............... 800 The beginning of the non-chronos \............... many kings, } ix., x. 840-947 The interval after the second woe, /............... 847-1521 The twelve hundred and sixty days of the woman, after she hath brought forth the man child, C xii. 6 947-1836 The third woe, 12 1058-1836 The time, times, and half a time, and \................... within that period, the beast, his forty}to xiii. 5 two months, his number 666, /................... 1209 War with the saints: the end of the chronos, 7 1614 An everlasting gospel promulged, xiv. 6 1810 The end of the forty-two months of the beast; after which, and the pouring out of the phials, he is not, and Babylon reigns queen, xv., xvi. 1832 The beast ascends from the bottomless pit, xvii., xviii. 1836 The end of the non-chronos, and of the many kings; the fulfilling of the word, and of the mystery of God; the repentance of the survivors in the great city; the end of the "little time," and of the three times and a half; the destruction of the east; the imprisonment of Satan, xix., xx. glossa.text: *Blessed are they that wash,* etc. Because he had said: Let him that hurts hurt, let him that is filthy be filthy still, lest any wicked man should say: Since I am wicked, why should I repent? he says. Not only are they blessed who spurn the greater persecution, but also those who have defiled their stoles which they received in baptism, if afterwards they shall have washed them, and it repent them that they have sinned.

*I Jesus.* John commended the book, through the angel, through his own dignity, now also through the authority of Christ himself. As if he should say: Let all that hear know *that I Jesus have sent my angel to testify to you these things. The bright star.* The clear star, that is, the great charity announcing the day, that is, the blessedness to come, through my resurrection wrought in the morning

*And the spirit,* that is, the Trinity, which for the excellence of its purity is called spirit: *And the spirit and the bride say,* etc. Here he adds also the testimony of the Trinity and of the faithful, as if: Therefore you ought to receive it, because the spirit and the bride, etc. *And he that thirsteth, let him come.* Yet not just anyone, but let him only come who thirsts: that is, who desires to believe. *He that will, let him take the water of life freely.* And it is no labour, because the will alone suffices.
*The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.* The consummation of the apostle in the word of Christ.

notes.text: For them who will believe — In all ages.
The glory which thou hast given me, I have given them — The glory of the only begotten shines in all the sons of God. How great is the majesty of Christians.

Here he returns to the apostles. I will — He asks, as having a right to be heard, and prays, not as a servant, but a Son: that they may behold my glory - Herein Is the happiness of heaven, 1 John iii, 2.
Righteous Father — The admission of believers to God through Christ, flows even from the justice of God.

I have declared to them thy name — Thy new, best name of love; that the love wherewith thou hast loved me - That thou and thy love, and I and my love, may be in them - That they may love me with that love.

glossa.text: *Not for them.* He now begins not concerning the apostles alone, or concerning the other members: but he does not pray for those who have already died in his faith, but for those who are in temptations. *But also for those who.* Even unto the end of the world, or [those who] already believe wherever they are, yet not so perfectly as they are to believe afterwards after the resurrection. *Through the word.* Through the word of the Gospel, which is theirs, not that it was preached through them only, but also through Paul and any others whatever, but because it was committed to them first and principally to be preached. This is the word of faith, the word of God, through which the thief believed, Paul believed, and whosoever believes.

*That all may be one.* He does not say, We all are one, but that they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me and I in thee, understand, we are one: so also the Father [is] in the Son and the Son in the Father, that they may be one, because of one substance. But we can be in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Or the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit can be in us; yet we cannot be one with God, because we are not of one substance. But God is in us as in a temple, we in him as a creature in the Creator. *That they also.* He says, in us, that what they are one by faith and charity they may ascribe to the grace of God, but that now light in the Lord.

*That the world.* The world is here taken for all those who are one. Nor does this, that they are, make a cause that they should believe, because rather by believing they are one; although they were one by nature, yet by dissenting from the One they were not one; but by praying he said that the world may believe, as by praying he said that all may be one, as if a third time it should be understood, I pray that the world may believe.

*Whom thou hast given.* That is, thou hast drawn them to me, so I also have chosen them out of the world: others are not given to him, are not his, although the power over all be his. *I will.* What the Almighty wills cannot fail to be done; but that is the will of the man, concerning which he says: *Not as I will ((Matth. XXVI))*. *That they may see.* When they shall have seen him, in the form of a servant made glorious, judging the good and the evil, the impious shall be taken away, that he may not see the glory of God whereby God is, which the clean of heart alone shall see, which will be to them life everlasting.

*That the love.* The love with which the Father loves the Son is in all the just, because they are his members and are loved in him who is wholly loved; therefore he subjoins: *And I am in them.* As if he should say: Because I am in them, he is in us in one way, as in a temple, we in him in another way; because we are he, since according to the man we are the body of his head.

hymns.title: Glorious things of thee are spoken
I will give you as a light to the nations
Lo, he comes with clouds descending
People look east. The time is near

praise.title: Light of the World (Here I Am to Worship)

echoes.text: There shall not be found with you anyone who makes his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, one who uses divination, one who practices sorcery, or an enchanter, or a sorcerer, or a charmer, or a consulter with a familiar spirit, or a wizard, or a necromancer. For whoever does these things is an abomination to Yahweh. Because of these abominations, Yahweh your God drives them out from before you.
echoes.note: The slave girl has a 'spirit of divination' (Greek: a python spirit) and earns money by fortune-telling. The Mosaic legislation expressly bans divination, soothsaying, and consulting spirits as abominations among the nations Israel dispossesses; Paul's exorcism enacts the abolition of precisely this pagan practice. Strong thematic and conceptual coherence with the core prohibition.

echoes.text: “‘Don’t turn to those who are mediums, nor to the wizards. Don’t seek them out, to be defiled by them. I am Yahweh your God.
echoes.note: 'Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards.' The girl's mantic spirit is the very category Israel is forbidden to consult; Paul's command silences and casts out the source. Reinforces the divination-prohibition cluster.

echoes.text: “‘The person that turns to those who are mediums, and to the wizards, to play the prostitute after them, I will even set my face against that person, and will cut him off from among his people.
echoes.note: The penalty against souls turning after mediums and familiar spirits; the pericope dramatizes the divine verdict on a profit-driven mantic spirit. Thematic recurrence within the Holiness Code's ban on spiritism.

echoes.text: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine: and he was priest of God Most High. He blessed him, and said, “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Abram gave him a tenth of all.
echoes.note: The spirit's cry that these are servants of 'the Most High God' (El Elyon) uses the divine title introduced by Melchizedek, God Most High, maker of heaven and earth; a Gentile-context title for the one true God now proclaimed (ironically) by a pagan spirit. Lexical-theological link to the El Elyon title-tradition.

echoes.text: Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet, and put him in the stocks that were in the upper gate of Benjamin, which was in Yahweh’s house.
echoes.note: The prophet Jeremiah is beaten and put in the stocks for proclaiming God's word; Paul and Silas, beaten with rods and fastened in stocks in the inner prison, replay the persecuted-prophet-in-stocks pattern. Strong situational coherence (beating + stocks for the word).

echoes.text: Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek me a woman who has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her.” His servants said to him, “Behold, there is a woman who has a familiar spirit at Endor.” Saul disguised himself, and put on other clothing, and went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, “Please divine to me by the familiar spirit, and bring me up whomever I shall name to you.” The woman said to him, […]
echoes.note: The medium of Endor as the canonical narrative instance of a woman trafficking in a familiar/divining spirit; the Philippian slave girl is its degraded Greco-Roman counterpart, here exposed and dispossessed. Narrative-typological resonance.

echoes.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace: he spoke and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you servants of the Most High God, come out, and come here. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the midst of the fire.
echoes.note: 'Servants of the Most High God' is the Septuagintal acclamation applied to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego by a pagan king; the slave girl's confession echoes this Gentile recognition of servants of God Most High. Verbal parallel to the title.

echoes.text: Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.
echoes.note: Joseph, falsely accused, is cast into the prison where the king's prisoners are bound, yet the LORD is with him; the righteous servant unjustly imprisoned and divinely vindicated prefigures Paul and Silas. Typological resonance setting up the deliverance.

echoes.text: It shall be, if the wicked man is worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his wickedness, by number. He may sentence him to no more than forty stripes. He shall not give more; lest, if he should give more, and beat him more than that many stripes, then your brother will be degraded in your sight.
echoes.note: The Mosaic regulation of judicial beating by a fixed number of stripes ('many stripes' laid on them) supplies the legal-cultural backdrop for the flogging, though here the Roman magistrates' beating is lawless. Conceptual link to the stripes motif.

echoes.text: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,
echoes.note: 'Thou puttest my feet in the stocks' as the poetic image of constraint by an adversary; the securing of Paul and Silas's feet in the stocks resonates with this Joban idiom of the afflicted righteous (cf. Job 33:11). Lexical (feet in stocks).

echoes.text: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and broke away their chains. Let them praise Yahweh for his loving kindness, for his wonderful works to the children of men! For he has broken the gates of brass, and cut through bars of iron.
echoes.note: God 'brought them out of darkness... and brake their bands in sunder,' for 'he hath broken the gates of brass, and cut the bars of iron in sunder.' The midnight earthquake that opens all the prison doors and looses everyone's bonds is the narrative enactment of this thanksgiving for the imprisoned whom God frees. Strong volume and thematic coherence; the controlling subtext for the deliverance.

echoes.text: who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry. Yahweh frees the prisoners.
echoes.note: 'The LORD looseth the prisoners' as a signature of God's saving character; the loosing of every prisoner's bonds dramatizes this divine attribute. Direct thematic match.

echoes.text: At midnight I will rise to give thanks to you, because of your righteous ordinances.
echoes.note: 'At midnight I will rise to give thanks unto thee.' Paul and Silas praying and singing hymns to God 'about midnight' closely matches the psalmist's nocturnal praise of the righteous sufferer who blesses God at the very hour of distress.

echoes.text: Then the earth shook and trembled. The foundations also of the mountains quaked and were shaken, because he was angry.
echoes.note: 'The earth shook and trembled; the foundations also of the hills moved and were shaken' in God's deliverance of his servant from enemies; the 'great earthquake' shaking 'the foundations of the prison' is the theophanic-rescue earthquake of the Davidic deliverance psalm. Lexical (foundations shaken) and thematic.

echoes.text: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
echoes.note: 'God my maker, who giveth songs in the night' as the wisdom theme of praise amid darkness; the midnight hymns of the prisoners embody songs given in the night. Conceptual parallel.

echoes.text: Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
echoes.note: The quaking of Sinai at God's descent supplies the theophany-as-earthquake background; the prison earthquake signals God's powerful presence. Thematic resonance, generic earthquake-theophany.

echoes.text: “I will go before you, and make the rough places smooth. I will break the doors of brass in pieces, and cut apart the bars of iron.
echoes.note: 'I will break in pieces the gates of brass, and cut in sunder the bars of iron' (to Cyrus); a second prophetic instance of God shattering prison/city barriers, reinforcing the Psalm 107 gate-breaking motif behind the opened doors. Recurrence of the broken-barriers theme.

echoes.text: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
echoes.note: The Servant's commission 'to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house'; the liberation of the jailer's prisoners realizes this servant-mission imagery. Thematic.

echoes.text: You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,
echoes.note: 'Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing'; the jailer who was about to kill himself ends 'rejoicing greatly with all his household,' the reversal-into-joy pattern of the deliverance psalms. Conceptual resonance for the turn from despair to rejoicing.

spans.label: Second journey
spans.note: Split with Barnabas; took Silas, picked up Timothy and Luke. Crossed into Europe at the Macedonian call — the Philippian jailer, the Areopagus, and a year and a half building the church at Corinth.

places.name: Derbe
places.id: Located at Kerti Hüyük north of Karaman, where a fourth-century inscription naming the bishop of Derbe was found in 1956. The southeastern terminus of the first missionary journey, on the Lycaonian / Cappadocian border.

places.name: Lystra
places.id: Generally located at Hatunsaray c. 30 km southwest of Konya, where a third-century inscription naming Lystra was found. A Roman colony refounded by Augustus c. 6 B.C. as part of the Pisidian-Galatian frontier defense.

places.name: Iconium
places.id: Modern Konya in central Anatolia, on the Anatolian plateau at the western edge of Lycaonia. Continuously inhabited from the Bronze Age; later the Seljuk capital. Acts assigns it variously to Phrygia (cf. v. 14:6) and Lycaonia, reflecting its position on the linguistic-administrative border.

places.name: Phrygia
places.id: The west-central Anatolian plateau, a cultural region split administratively between Roman Asia (west) and Galatia (east) in the apostolic period. Pisidian Antioch and Iconium lay within the wider Phrygian zone.

places.name: Galatia
places.id: The Roman province (formed 25 B.C.) covering north-central Anatolia, named for the Celtic tribes (Galatae) settled there in the third century B.C. The province at its largest also included Pisidia, Lycaonia, and parts of Phrygia — which is why Acts can locate Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe variously in 'Galatia' and in Lycaonia.

places.name: Asia
places.id: The Roman province (formed 129 B.C.) covering the western third of Anatolia, with Ephesus as its capital and the seven cities of Revelation 1-3 within its bounds. Distinct from 'Asia' as a continent and from the Seleucid use of the term for the wider Anatolian-Syrian sphere.

places.name: Mysia
places.id: The northwestern region of Anatolia, between Bithynia (north), Lydia and Phrygia (south), and the Aegean and Hellespont (west). Administratively part of Roman Asia. Troas lies within Mysia at its northwestern corner.

places.name: Bithynia
places.id: The Roman province on the southern Black Sea coast (Asia Minor), combined with Pontus from 63 B.C. Capital at Nicomedia. Pliny the Younger’s correspondence with Trajan c. A.D. 110 was written from this province.

places.name: Troas
places.id: Alexandria Troas on the Aegean coast of Mysia, founded by Antigonus c. 310 B.C. and refounded by Lysimachus. A Roman colony from c. 12 B.C. The natural embarkation port for crossings to Macedonia. Distinct from the Homeric Troy / Hisarlik some 30 km to the north.

places.name: Macedonia
places.id: The Roman province (formed 146 B.C.) covering northern Greece, the Vardar/Axios valley, and adjacent territories. Capital at Thessalonica from 27 B.C. The 'Macedonian vision' of Acts 16:9 brings the gospel into Europe for the first time.

places.name: Samothrace
places.id: A small mountainous island in the northern Aegean, c. 60 km off the Thracian coast. Famous in antiquity for the Sanctuary of the Great Gods (the Cabeiroi); the Hellenistic Winged Victory of Samothrace was carved here. The standard overnight stop for ships crossing from Troas to Neapolis.

places.name: Neapolis
places.id: On the Macedonian coast c. 14 km southeast of Philippi, modern Kavala. The harbor served Philippi and was the standard western terminus of the sea route from Asia Minor.

places.name: Philippi
places.id: On a hill above the Egnatian Way c. 14 km inland from Neapolis, refounded by Philip II of Macedon (hence the name) on the older site of Krenides. A Roman colony (Colonia Augusta Iulia Philippensis) from 42 B.C. after the battle of Philippi where Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius. The 'foremost city of the district' in v. 16:12.

places.name: Thyatira
places.id: Modern Akhisar in western Anatolia (Roman Asia), a centre of guild industry famous for purple-dye production (cf. Lydia, the ‘seller of purple’, v. 16:14). One of the seven cities addressed in Revelation 2:18-29.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...” Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim/f + cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10./f* at the east of the garden of […]
echoes.note: Right to the tree of life and entry restored — direct reversal of the barred access after Eden's expulsion. Coherence with 22:2; the 'right to the tree of life' is the Edenic inheritance regranted.

echoes.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.
echoes.note: 'A shoot from the stump of Jesse, a branch from his roots.' Source for 'the root... of David.' Davidic-messianic root imagery; coherence with Rev 5:5. LXX 'rhiza' matches 'root.'

echoes.text: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.
echoes.note: 'The root of Jesse, who shall stand as a signal to the peoples; him shall the nations seek.' Direct source for 'the root... of David' as the messianic ensign; LXX explicit 'rhiza tou Iessai.'

echoes.text: I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and break down all the sons of Sheth.
echoes.note: Balaam: 'a star shall come out of Jacob, a scepter shall rise out of Israel.' Source for 'the Bright and Morning Star' as messianic title. Strong messianic-star tradition (also at Qumran); coherence with Rev 2:28.

echoes.text: “Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
echoes.note: 'Everyone who thirsts, come to the waters... without money and without price.' Direct source for 'He who is thirsty, let him come... take the water of life freely (dorean).' Strong verbal + thematic. LXX dorean matches.

echoes.text: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Come, let us walk in the light of the LORD' — invitation-to-come framing; faint background to the threefold 'Come!' Generic invitation idiom.

echoes.text: You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute, or the wages of a male prostitute, into the house of Yahweh your God for any vow; for both of these are an abomination to Yahweh your God.
echoes.note: 'Dogs' excluded from the assembly (the 'wages of a dog' barred from the house of the LORD) — possible background for 'Outside are the dogs.' Conceptual; the metaphor is debated.

echoes.text: Open to me the gates of righteousness. I will enter into them. I will give thanks to Yah. This is the gate of Yahweh; the righteous will enter into it.
echoes.note: 'Open to me the gates of righteousness... this is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.' Faint background for the righteous entering by the gates into the city. Conceptual.

echoes.text: Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter: the one which keeps faith.
echoes.note: 'Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter in.' Reinforces the gates-entry-of-the-righteous motif behind 'enter in by the gates into the city.' Faint.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: and I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all; and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all;
echoes.note: 'That they may all be one' / 'perfected into one' (vv21-23) figures Ezekiel's promise 'I will make them one nation... and one king shall be king over them all.' The unification of God's scattered people under one head is a coherent, recurrent figural backdrop for the Johannine unity petitions.

echoes.text: and join them for you one to another into one stick, that they may become one in your hand.
echoes.note: The two sticks 'joined... one in your hand' is the enacted sign behind repeated 'that they may be one' (vv21-22). Reinforces the Ezekiel reunification channel introduced at v11; coherent and recurrent, figural rather than verbal.

echoes.text: For then I will purify the lips of the peoples, that they may all call on Yahweh’s name, to serve him shoulder to shoulder.
echoes.note: Peoples serving the LORD 'with one accord' echoes the unity 'that the world may believe' (vv21-23). The purified-and-unified-nations motif coheres with the missional aim of the unity but the Volume is faint.

echoes.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him. When Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come near him. Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses spoke to them. […]
echoes.note: 'The glory which you have given me, I have given to them' (v22) faintly mirrors Moses' face shining with reflected divine glory after Sinai. The motif of communicated/derivative glory is coherent, but John speaks of indwelling glory rather than facial radiance; low Volume.

echoes.text: For you have made him a little lower than God, and crowned him with glory and honor.
echoes.note: Glory bestowed on the disciples (v22) loosely recalls humanity 'crowned with glory and honor.' Generic glory-conferral idiom; supportive but faint and contested.

echoes.text: Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
echoes.note: 'You... loved them, even as you loved me' (v23) echoes the LORD setting his love on Israel not for their greatness but because he loved them. The gratuitous divine love for the elect community coheres with the prayer, though John extends it to the disciples through the Son; low Volume.

echoes.text: “Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed. When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born; while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world. When he established the heavens, I was […]
echoes.note: 'You loved me before the foundation of the world' and 'see my glory' (v24) figure the Son after Wisdom delighted in by God before creation. The pre-cosmic love/glory shared between Father and agent is the same Wisdom channel that frames v5; coherent and recurrent within the prayer.

echoes.text: Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God.
echoes.note: 'Before the foundation of the world' (v24) reuses the pre-creation eternity idiom of 'from everlasting... before... you had formed the earth.' Matches the temporal frame asserted of the Father-Son love and glory; moderate Volume via the recurring formula.

echoes.text: He said, “Please show me your glory.”
echoes.note: 'That they may see my glory' (v24) figures Moses' request 'Show me your glory' and the Sinai vision tradition. John transposes the longed-for sight of divine glory into the disciples' eschatological seeing of the Son's glory; coherent with the chapter's glory and Name theology.

echoes.text: but let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I knew you' (v25) recalls the LORD who 'practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness' and the boast of knowing him from 9:23-24. The righteousness-plus-knowledge cluster ties v25 back to v3's eternal-life-as-knowledge; coherent, moderate Volume.

echoes.text: He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.”
echoes.note: 'I made known to them your name, and will make it known' (v26) reprises 'I will proclaim before you my name, the LORD,' closing the inclusio with v6. The ongoing proclamation of the Name as the vehicle of God's presence and love is coherent and recurrent across the prayer.

echoes.text: I will sanctify my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you have profaned in their midst; and the nations shall know that I am Yahweh, says the Lord Yahweh, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes.
echoes.note: 'I made known to them your name... that the love... may be in them' (v26) resonates with God's resolve to 'vindicate the holiness of my great name' so the nations know him, paired in Ezekiel with the indwelling Spirit (36:26-27). The hallowing-of-the-Name leading to interior transformation coheres with John's Name-and-indwelling climax; moderate Volume.

echoes.text: I will declare your name to my brothers. In the midst of the assembly, I will praise you.
echoes.note: 'I made known to them your name, and will make it known' (v26) restates the psalmist's vow 'I will tell of your name to my brothers,' bracketing the prayer with v6. The repeated declaration of the Name to the community gives strong Coherence and Recurrence within John.

echoes.text: Pour out your wrath on the nations that don’t know you; on the kingdoms that don’t call on your name;
echoes.note: 'The world has not known you' (v25) echoes 'the nations that do not know you,' the contrast between God's people and the ignorant nations. Coherent with John's world/disciples antithesis but the phrasing is generic; low Volume.

echoes.text: My holy name will I make known in the midst of my people Israel; neither will I allow my holy name to be profaned any more: and the nations shall know that I am Yahweh, the Holy One in Israel.
echoes.note: 'I made known to them your name' (v26) echoes 'I will make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel.' Reinforces the make-known-the-Name channel alongside Exod 33 and Isa 52:6; lower independent Volume, contested.

harmony.note: Five chapters where the Synoptics give the meal: the new commandment, the vine, the Paraclete, and the high-priestly prayer. John only.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Father, may they all be one, as you and I are one,
that the world may believe you sent me.
At midnight in the prison they sang, and the doors flew open;
the chains fell off, and the jailer's whole house was saved.
The Spirit and the bride say, Come. Surely I am coming soon.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Listen for the singing that rises at midnight from the deepest cell, where two men sit with their feet in the stocks.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
The ground shakes, the doors fly open, the chains fall off — and not one prisoner runs.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
By dawn the jailer and his whole household have gone down into the water, and there is a feast in the prison-keeper's house.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
This is the prayer the Lord prayed over us: that we may all be one, that the world may believe.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
The Spirit and the bride cry Come, and the thirsty answer Come, and we lift the old glad shout:
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Father, make us one, as you and the Son are one.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
At midnight the prisoners sing, and the doors fly open.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
The chains fall off, and a whole household is saved.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
The Spirit and the bride say, Come. Surely he is coming soon.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
